I think about this year like I thought about last year. My land is 6 mu — same as always. I plant wheat in October, then maize after wheat harvest in June. This is what my father did, what my neighbors do, what I do.

For seeds, I buy from the shop in town. Everyone around here uses the hybrid maize seed — Zhengdan or whatever the dealer has that year. For wheat I use the improved seed the shop sells, same as my neighbors. I don't save seed anymore, the shop seed grows better.

For fertilizer, I go by bags. For wheat, I put down 2 bags of compound fertilizer before planting — that's about 100 kg on each mu, the big 50 kg bags. Then in spring when the wheat is greening up, I spread 1 bag of urea per mu, maybe a bit more. Urea is 46% nitrogen, I know this because the dealer told me years ago. For maize, same idea — 2 bags compound at planting, then urea at big trumpet stage, about 25-30 kg per mu. If I put less, I worry the leaves turn yellow and I lose grain. Fertilizer costs money but losing harvest costs more. My neighbor Old Wang tried using less last year and his yield was lower than mine, so I keep doing what I do.

Water — I have the well. Wheat I water before winter, then in spring when it jointing, then at grain filling. Three times usually, sometimes four if the spring is dry. Maize needs less water because summer rains come, but I water once or twice if it gets dry in July.

For pesticide, I spray when I see bugs. Wheat gets one spray for aphids in spring, sometimes two. Maize I spray once for borers. I don't spray if I don't see problems.

Tillage — I hire the rotary tiller machine from the village, it comes through and works the field. No more ploughing by hand like when I was young.

My yield is usually around 450 kg wheat and 550 kg maize per mu. Good years a bit more, bad years less. I don't expect miracles, I just want a normal harvest.
